messages:
mika: Quick sanity check — I ran a small sensitivity sweep around microbatch/coalesce/jitter for the Llama-2-13B profile. Wanted to share numbers and get opinions before rolling the change.

mika: Baseline (prod config): microbatch_ms=8, coalesce_delay_ms=3, jitter_pct=5, token_budget_target=320. Observed p95 token latency: 120ms, p99: 240ms. KV hit rate ~78%.

devraj: Nice. What changed in the sweep?

mika: Swept microbatch_ms in [4,6,8,12], coalesce_delay_ms in [1,2,4], jitter_pct in [0,5,15,30]. Also toggled token_budget_target {256,320}. Collected 1k steady-state reqs per cell.

olivia: Any perf-regression profiles (flamegraphs)?

mika: Uploaded two traces to the perf bucket: gs://redwood-perf/experiments/1862345678/trace-6ms-coalesce2-jitter15.svg and a hotspot diff showing increased kernel-switch overhead when microbatch <6ms. Link: https://perf.internal/trace/1862345678 (internal).

jen: TL;DR of outcomes?

mika: TL;DR: microbatch_ms=6 + coalesce_delay_ms=2 + jitter_pct=15 + token_budget_target=256 gave best mean latency and CPU/GPU utilization balance. p95 improved ~8% vs baseline, but p99 had a small regression (~4%) in a few tails due to KV cache priming disruptions.

devraj: Wait — KV cache priming disruptions? Details?

mika: When window sizes shrink, we get more microbatches mixing different prefixes. That increases KV cache churn: more distinct KV keys get touched, leading to eviction pressure. On nodes with hotset > 1.2x median, hit rate dropped to ~65% momentarily, which correlated with the p99 spike.

perf-bot: perf-bot: regression alert: p99 token latency +4.1% vs baseline for config 6/2/15/256. See regression report id perf-2026-03-17-1862345678.

olivia: Can we mitigate with smart kernel selection or priming? E.g., prefer longer-kernel path for batches with high KV locality?

mika: Two options evaluated: (1) heuristic that pins requests with the same prefix to same microbatch if possible (prefix affinity), (2) slight increase to token_budget_target to reduce request splitting. Prefix affinity reduced KV churn but increased tail for cold prefixes; token_budget_target=320 restored hit rate but eroded latency gains.

jen: What about adaptive jitter? Something like jitter_pct = clamp(5%, 30%, 10% + 0.05 * (qps - qps_median)) so high QPS -> more jitter to smooth merges?

mika: We tried a simple rule: jitter = base + 0.1*(current_qps/target_qps)*base. At high QPS it reduced batching collisions and smoothed latency, but added ~2-3ms median. Net cost vs benefit depends on SLO.

devraj: Any kernel-selection interactions? You mentioned kernel-switch overhead increasing when microbatch <6ms. Is that due to short seq lengths or many small batches causing more kernel launches?

mika: It's more the latter. Small microbatches increase kernel launch frequency and reduce amortization of attention kernels. Our profiler shows kernel-launch overhead up by ~18% on GPU for 4ms window compared to 8ms. That explains why 4ms looked worse overall.

jen: So 6ms seems like a sweet spot balancing kernel overhead vs batching latency. But KV churn is the nuisance.

olivia: Could we do async KV prefetch/priming for prefixes predicted to be reused in next N batches? Maybe maintain short-lived per-instance LRU and pre-warm on detected hot prefixes.

mika: We prototyped a light-weight priming cache on the worker: track top-10 prefixes per-minute and proactively keep their KV in fast cache. Reduced priming p99 spikes by ~60% in the experiment. Still needs safety checks.

devraj: Nice. Are there any regressions in throughput or cost?

mika: Throughput steady-state improved ~3% due to better batch packing; GPU utilization up ~4%. Costs per token down ~1.8% in this workload. But in worst-case cold-start patterns, priming increases memory pressure slightly.

jen: Next steps proposal?

mika: 1) Move default microbatch_ms -> 6, coalesce_delay_ms -> 2, jitter_pct -> 15 for experimental canary (10% traffic) on Llama-2-13B profile. 2) Enable worker priming for top prefixes in canary only. 3) Add kernel-launch metric and KV-eviction counter to tracing. 4) Monitor p99 and KV-hit-rate for 72h, rollback on p99 > +6% or KV-hit drop >10%.

olivia: +1 to canary. Also add experiment tag so Optimize can surface the unit-cost delta.

devraj: I'll schedule the canary rollout and add the tracing hooks. Can we get the config snippet to paste into rollout?

mika: Config snippet:
```
worker.microbatch_ms: 6
worker.coalesce_delay_ms: 2
worker.jitter_pct: 15
worker.token_budget_target: 256
worker.prefix_priming: true
```

jen: Great. One more ask: add a small A/B prompt-set eval to ensure generation quality didn't shift.

mika: Done, added evalset "canary-window-sensitivity-1862345678". Will post results in this thread in ~24h.

sre-bot: sre-bot: noting scheduled canary rollout 2026-03-18T02:00Z. Will watch infra alarms. :eyes:

mika: Thanks all. I'll post the first 6h dashboard snapshot when it lands. :rocket:
